prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This manifesto centers on withdrawing from the European Union and reclaiming control over laws, borders, trade, and budget contributions. It proposes binding national and local referenda, recall of MPs, an AV+ electoral system, elected county-level Police, Health, and Education Boards, and abolishing regional government bodies. Devolved assemblies would be staffed by the same Westminster MPs from each nation, with English-only sittings.

Tax and economy: raise the income tax threshold to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat tax merging income tax and employee NI, with pension income below higher-rate kept at 20%; phase out employers’ NI over five years; cut quangos and reduce the public sector to roughly 1997 size; replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax sharing revenue with councils; return half of local business rates to councils; abolish inheritance tax when feasible. Financial regulation would return to the Bank of England, capital ratios rise to at least 8%, retail and investment banking would be separated, and a lending “corset” reinstated.

Jobs and industry: long-term programs to create skilled jobs via enhanced defence procurement, a 25-year nuclear build, £30bn over 10 years on flood/coastal defences, major transport investment, and prison construction; establish Production Enterprise Centres; university and FE funding replaced by student/training vouchers; amend takeover rules to protect strategic firms; scrap carbon trading and similar schemes.

Immigration and asylum: a five-year freeze on permanent settlement, then a tightly controlled, points-based system targeting no more than 50,000 annually; time-limited work permits; visas with health insurance for non-work visitors; tripled border staffing; no amnesty for illegal immigrants; enforcement of first safe country rules and secure processing centers; repeal the Human Rights Act and withdraw from the ECHR; reintroduce the Primary Purpose Rule.

Law and order: elected Police Boards; “life means life” sentencing; double prison capacity and end early release; a “three strikes” policy; stronger homeowner self-defence rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; boot camps for youth offenders; abolish the CPS.

Defence: increase spending by 40% (about 1% of GDP), expand the Army and TA, restore Navy strength with three carriers, increase RAF lift/rotary assets and JSF numbers, maintain and later replace Trident submarines, cut MOD bureaucracy, and prioritise NATO.

NHS: protect frontline services; elected Health Boards; reduce layers of management; franchise services within fixed budgets; optional health vouchers to exit the NHS; restore clinical leadership and on-the-job nurse training; restore free eye tests and dental check-ups.

Education: school vouchers; retain and expand grammar/professional schools; broader aptitude testing; higher standards for teacher training; end the 50% university target and social engineering rules; shift some universities to vocational focus; grants via vouchers; franchise schools; lighter national curriculum; stronger discipline; support special schools and home education.

Pensions and welfare: a flat, non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week at 65; target pension tax relief at low/middle earners; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unfunded public-sector schemes; simplify benefits into a Basic Cash Benefit; merge child benefits; create nursery vouchers; restrict benefits to citizens or those resident 5+ years; introduce community “workfare.”

Foreign trade: leave the EU’s political structures; seek a Swiss-style FTA; regain an independent WTO seat; pursue Commonwealth and other global trade deals.

Energy/environment: expand nuclear to up to 50% of electricity; support cleaner coal; prioritize offshore wind, repeal the Climate Change Act and EU carbon schemes; invest in EVs and rail electrification; increase flood/coastal defences.

Transport: invest £3bn/year in infrastructure; build bypasses and widen roads; fuel duty “windfall return”; Britdisc for foreign lorries; three new high-speed rail lines; reopen routes; longer rail franchises; shift freight to rail/canals; oppose further Heathrow expansion in favor of a Thames Estuary airport.

Housing/planning: emphasize demand reduction via immigration control; use empty homes; scrap regional strategies and the Infrastructure Planning Commission; binding local referenda on major schemes; elected Green Belt management; remove certain development levies; support social housing via council bonds; end business rates on empty premises.

Culture and other: protect traditional measures and key brands; curriculum on national contributions; measures on extremist preaching and face coverings in specified settings; a Commonwealth Day holiday; English Parliament and St George’s Day holiday. Agriculture/fishing: leave the CAP/CFP, retain support during transition, expand labeling and co-ops, set a 200-mile EEZ, land all catches, ban industrial fishing. Commitments include animal welfare, supporting Royal Mail/Post Offices, designated pub smoking rooms, and small business support.
